thread:
anya: Heads-up — we're seeing attributed quota bounce to tenant A when requests come from proxy B using delegated service tokens. Dashboard shows project A billed but origin was proj-proxy-B.
liam: ugh. can you paste an example request/headers?
anya: sure: 
```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer sa-token:delegated
X-Origin-Project: proj-proxy-B
X-Forwarded-For: 10.2.3.4
```
sheila: do we currently trust any X-Origin-Project header from the edge?
mike: no, we canonicalize origin from our auth-exchange service. the proxy isn't doing exchange correctly for delegated tokens.
anya: right — proxy B attaches X-Origin-Project but we ignore it and use token.project which is the underlying service-account owner (proj-A). results: billing + quota go to proj-A.
liam: why does proxy not exchange? is it a config flag missing on the proxy side?
mike: proxy expected downstream to call /auth/exchange?source=proxy but it forwarded tokens raw (fast-path) to keep latency low.
sheila: that's the UX tradeoff again. we can either: 1) require explicit exchange (safest), 2) accept signed origin header (needs sig verification), or 3) derive origin via token introspect with proxy identity mapping.
anya: option 2 seems lightweight: proxy signs origin with its key and we verify on authz. happy path: low-latency and correct attribution. downside: key management + replay risk.
liam: for rollout, can we gate on a console flag per-proxy? so we only accept signed-origin from proxy B if enabled.
mike: yep. add telemetry event when signed-origin accepted vs rejected. want counts, false positives, and latency delta.
sheila: also add dashboard split: "billing attribution" vs "effective origin" so SREs can see mismatches.
anya: agreed. propose: start with (a) short spec, (b) proxy side change to sign X-Origin-Project with header `X-Origin-Sig`, (c) auth service verify signature and populate origin_claim if valid, (d) console shows mismatch and a migration flag `accept_signed_origin`.
liam: small nit — make the header name `X-Redwood-Origin` and signature `X-Redwood-Origin-Sig` to avoid collisions.
mike: good call. I'll draft the auth PR and add metrics: auth.origin.accepted, auth.origin.rejected, auth.origin.mismatch.
sheila: for rollout plan: enable flag in staging for proxy B only, monitor metrics for 48h, then enable in prod for that proxy. we need a rollback playbook if mismatch spike > 0.5% of requests.
anya: sounds good. can someone add a short console mock for the dashboard split?
liam: I'll sketch a mock today and post in #design later. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: new deploy queued: auth-service@edge-origin-sign-check -> canary to staging (tag: origin-sig-v1).
mike: launching canary now. will post results in 1h.
anya: thanks all — this should fix a few unbilled proxies and noisy quota owners. :rocket:
